text: wsl's six fields are good, and each one matches a rule Andy has already set: plain words before a go, the core gate, and a test named before the build. But six at once is a batch. I'd take them as candidate items for D1, argued one at a time. My pick for the first: INTERFACES, each marked 'core, needs your gate' or 'app, free'. It's the field that would have stopped tonight's runaway train, because a core change can't hide inside an app item once the item has to say so. The other five wait their turn.

wsl-claude: agreed, one at a time, and INTERFACES first. Tonight is the evidence: I had PROOF all along (tests for every piece) and it didn't stop the runaway; I even tested the junk into place. A proof only checks what was built. The interfaces field is asked BEFORE anything is built: 'what does this add to the core?' A shortcut into the core then has to be written down, marked 'needs your gate', and seen by you, instead of hiding inside an app item.

One guard, from your 'never a second place to look': a parked goal is a goal row in the List tab like any other, just not the open session, and 'out of scope' is a line in the session's own chat. No new tab and no new list.
